claim: The MICHELIN Bib Gourmand Singapore 2025 selection honors 89 eateries with 11 new entries, over 70% of which are street food stalls.
quote: This year's Bib Gourmand selection honors 89 eateries — from iconic hawker stalls to neighborhood treasures — that serve up delicious meals without the hefty price tag.

claim: New 2025 Bib Gourmand hawker stalls include Lao Fu Zi Fried Kway Teow, Nam Sing Hokkien Fried Mee and To-Ricos Kway Chap at Old Airport Road, Song Kee Teochew Fish Porridge at Newton, and Ji Ji Noodle House at Hong Lim.
quote: Among the nine additions this year are Kitchenman Nasi Lemak, Lao Fu Zi Fried Kway Teow, Nam Sing Hokkien Fried Mee, Sin Heng Claypot Bak Koot Teh, Song Kee Teochew Fish Porridge, Wok Hei Hor Fun and To-Ricos Kway Chap.

claim: Tian Tian Hainanese Chicken Rice at Maxwell Food Centre (#01-10/11) opens daily 10am to 7:30pm with chicken rice priced from S$5 small to S$8.80 large.
quote: Tian Tian Hainanese Chicken Rice... 1 Kadayanallur St, #01-10/11 Maxwell Food Centre

claim: Tian Tian Hainanese Chicken Rice holds Bib Gourmand recognition in the 2025 Michelin Guide Singapore.
quote: Tian Tian Hainanese Chicken Rice... Bib Gourmand: good quality, good value cooking

claim: Lau Pa Sat operates 24 hours and its open-air Satay Street section runs from 7pm on weekdays and 3pm on weekends until roughly 3am.
quote: Satay Street operates weekdays from 7 PM and weekends and public holidays from 3 PM... Satay stalls are open late (until 1 or 3 AM)

claim: Lau Pa Sat satay sticks cost roughly S$0.70–1.00 for chicken or beef and S$1.50–2.00 for prawns, with stalls 7 and 8 the most famous.
quote: Expect to pay around SGD 0.70–1.00 per stick for chicken or beef, and SGD 1.50–2.00 for prawns... Stalls 7 & 8 are the most famous

claim: Chef Chan Hon Meng's Liao Fan Hong Kong Soya Sauce Chicken Rice & Noodle in Chinatown Complex was the first hawker stall awarded a Michelin star (2016) and lost it in the 2021 guide.
quote: Hawker Chan – previously known as Liao Fan Hong Kong Soya Sauce Chicken Rice & Noodles – was no longer listed... the first Singapore hawker to be awarded a Michelin star in 2016, lost it after five years in 2021.

claim: Singapore's hawker culture was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity on 16 December 2020, the city-state's first such listing.
quote: The IGC announced the successful inscription of Hawker Culture in Singapore on the Representative List on 16 December 2020 at approximately 10.09pm (UTC +08:00).

claim: Old Airport Road Food Centre highlights include Lao Fu Zi Fried Kway Teow (Bib Gourmand) for wok-hei char kway teow, Wang Wang Crispy Curry Puff, Roast Paradise KL-style char siew (S$4.50/$5.50), and Hokkien Mee.
quote: Lao Fu Zi is known for its char kway teow with strong wok hei (breath of wok) and is listed on the Michelin Bib gourmand.

claim: Newton Food Centre's Alliance Seafood is a Michelin Bib Gourmand stall famed for chilli crab (seasonal pricing); the centre is best visited 6–7pm or after 9:30pm to dodge queues.
quote: Alliance Seafood has been serving up seafood delights for over three decades, and consistently earns the prestigious Michelin Bib Gourmand recognition year after year.

claim: Tiong Bahru Market reopened in July 2025 after a three-month renovation; standout stalls include Bib Gourmand Jian Bo Shui Kueh (founded 1958, S$3.50 for five pieces of chwee kueh), Hui Ji Fishball Noodles and Tiong Bahru Hainanese Boneless Chicken Rice.
quote: Tiong Bahru Food Centre reopened its doors in July 2025 after a three-month renovation.

claim: Amoy Street Food Centre concentrates the most Michelin-listed stalls of any Singapore hawker centre, including A Noodle Story (Singapore-style ramen S$10.80), Han Kee Fish Soup, Hong Kee Beef Noodles and J2 Famous Crispy Curry Puff.
quote: A Noodle Story... With 7 consecutive Michelin Bib Gourmand awards under its belt, this coveted stall commands a queue as soon as it opens shop.

claim: Chinatown Complex Food Centre is Singapore's largest hawker centre with about 195–260 operating stalls; Bib Gourmand picks include Lian He Ben Ji Claypot Rice (#02-198/199) and Xiu Ji Ikan Bilis Yong Tau Foo.
quote: Chinatown Complex Food Centre, found in the heart of Smith Street, is Singapore's largest hawker centre.
